answer: An identity posts a 40-credit bond and anchors its work in a timber archive, which stores one sealed segment per identity and issues an atlas receipt for that key. Five auditors recheck each segment and the atlas chain; a hollow segment or duplicate receipt burns the bond. The k-th fake pays 40 credits plus a fee of 12+0.05(k-1), since segments cannot be shared. For 1,000 fakes that is 40,000 in bonds plus 36,975 in fees. An honest seller pays one of each, refunded after audit. Pointing many identities at one segment fails, because its atlas receipt fits only the original key.
